evidence: Source-level check passes: frozen workbook Quality Checks!35 says interactive/time-varying/viewport behavior must be exercised; Internal Quality Checks!35 has no extra annotation. The frozen quality procedure at references/quality-checks.md:142-143 asks that judges be told to click, wait, resize or toggle as applicable. The render gate at tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23 requires a real keyboard-authored Run and two clicks that produce increasing totals, excluding a decorative dead button. Functional tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:158 requires a live HTML button update; :176 changes an input and canvas through ordinary controls before recovery; :185 establishes a working timer, waits for a visible time-limit reason, supersedes or Stops a delayed marker, and requires no later old marker. Polish tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23 requires real keyboard traversal and visible focus; :32 inspects feedback after successful and invalid actions. All five prompt.md files instruct Playwright MCP and real browser interaction. Public instruction.md and the six environment/instructions notes contain no mobile, responsive, resize, theme or animation promise; tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:24,34 explicitly score desktop appearance, so a conforming desktop-only app is not failed for lacking an unrequested mobile layout. A broken first-paint-only app could not satisfy the render click result or editor/timer action criteria. Source hashes for the cited frozen task/rules files match manifest.json and input_sha256; the workbook hash is 6d44970b2ff67fefad1e2327e743fc226fcd4c50ff55baf899f41069a9b3fd7f. Risk remains because raw-evidence-index.json and actual configured judge action logs are absent; preflight.json is source checking, not observation that judges executed the steps. The delayed-marker clause implies later observation but does not specify a post-supersession wait beyond the chosen callback delay, so actual judge behavior should be checked when logs exist. No Oracle, target-model or portal result is inferred.
